item.title: Stacks of Parabolic Vector Bundles in the Geometric Langlands Program
item.description: arXiv:2611.31485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: I define a locus inside stacks of parabolic vector bundles on smooth projective curves which is important for the construction of twisted Hecke eigensheaves in the ramified geometric Langlands program for $\mathrm{GL}_n$. I give an explicit description of this locus in the case of rank $3$ parabolic vector bundles on $\mathbb{P}^1$ with parabolic structure at four points. This example involves partial flags in the level structure as well as a non-trivial twisted equivariance condition.
item.dc:creator: Paul Siemon

item.title: An Introduction to Semialgebraic Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.31550v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The first chapter of these lecture notes explains algorithms for counting real roots and the Tarski-Seidenberg theorem. In the next two chapters we study semialgebraic subsets of $\mathbb R^n$ , which are defined by boolean combinations of polynomial equations and inequalities. The main tool for this study is the cylindrical algebraic decomposition, which is introduced in Chapter 2. The principal result of Chapter 3 is the triangulation theorem. This theorem shows that semialgebraic sets have a simple topology, which can be effectively computed from their definitions. Chapter 4 contains examples of finiteness results and uniform bounds for semialgebraic families. In particular, we give an explicit bound for the number of connected components of a real algebraic set as a function of the degree of the equations and the dimension of the ambient space.
item.dc:creator: Michel Coste

item.title: On the unirationality of anticanonical weighted complete intersection surfaces: the infinite families
item.description: arXiv:2611.31552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Anticanonical weighted complete intersection surfaces fall into finitely many sporadic families and four infinite families. We prove that the anticanonical surfaces lying in the infinite families are unirational over their field of definition. Over a Hilbertian field, we further prove that a Hilbert subset of members consists of nonrational surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Giulia Gugiatti, Alex Massarenti

item.title: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties II. Fibrations over a polarized base
item.description: arXiv:2611.31691v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We extend the height and energy inequalities for fibrations over curves to a fibration $f:X\to Y$ over a polarized variety $(Y,B)$. For an integrable relatively nef adelic line bundle $\bar L$, we prove a height inequality under the assumption that $L$ is nef on the inverse image of a geometric generic complete-intersection curve in $Y$. We deduce a lower bound for the local energy at almost every complex or nonarchimedean realization of a fixed polarized model when $L$ is $f$-ample. For a slope semistable bundle on a fixed polarized complex variety, we show that the infimum of the energy on its projective bundle equals the infimum of Donaldson's functional on Hermitian quotient metrics, with the normalization given below.
item.dc:creator: Shou-Wu Zhang

item.title: Schubert positivity for filtered bundles
item.description: arXiv:2611.31862v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We characterize formal filtered nefness of a formal quotient flag on a polarized Hodge--Lefschetz module by the formal nefness of its positive-rank total quotients. Using this criterion, we prove that quotient Schubert functors preserve formal nefness and that Schubert incidence modules inherit every commuting formally filtered nef flag. As geometric and numerical consequences, we recover the positivity criteria of Fulton--Lazarsfeld and Fulton and extend the Lorentzian polynomial theorem of Lu and Zheng to derived Schubert classes of filtered bundles. In combinatorics, our framework applies to tautological flags of flag matroids on ordinary and augmented matroid Chow rings as well as on the intersection cohomology of rational projective fans equipped with a common weight map. We deduce concordance-sensitive intersection inequalities, establish the Schubert positivity of the leading Riemann--Roch Chow class of a flag matroid, and show that the nonvanishing supports of derived Schubert numbers on an augmented Chow ring form the Higgs lifts of an intrinsically determined matroid quotient.
item.dc:creator: Enhan Li

item.title: Full Support For the Degree-Zero Hitchin Morphism
item.description: arXiv:2611.32052v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a draft argument for the full-support conjecture for the canonical GLn Hitchin morphism in degree zero over a smooth complex projective curve of genus at least two. The whole-base Ng\^o support equality yields a finite necessary classification in terms of weighted products of maximal equigeneric spectral-factor families. We study their generic nodality, develop moving-cycle arguments for arbitrary multiplicities, and give an intersection calculation using generalized parabolic presentations and intrinsic Nash transforms. We relate the full-base Ng\^o string to the BPS formula for intersection Hodge numbers in every rank and give the genus-two rank-three Hodge table. The arguments developed here are presented for mathematical checking and revision by the authors. And the article is generated by ChatGPT, the author is trying his best to comprehense the article and the human's version is coming soon.
item.dc:creator: Zuoyang Chen

item.title: Chern classes of vanishing cycles for maps having no blowups
item.description: arXiv:2611.32080v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the nearby and vanishing cycles for maps with no blowups. For holomorphic maps between complex manifolds admitting at most ICIS, we show that the Riemann-Hurwitz defect in Chern classes is compensated for by the Chern class transformation of the Milnor number constructible function.
item.dc:creator: Xia Liao

item.title: Simultaneous Waring problems for binary forms and the geometry of rational curves
item.description: arXiv:2611.32267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the simultaneous Waring problem for binary forms and its geometric applications to rational curves. By analyzing the minimal free resolution of the simultaneous annihilator, we establish formulas for both simultaneous Waring ranks and border Waring ranks including explicit computations for binary monomials. As a geometric application, we explicitly describe parametrizations of rational curves up to projective equivalence. We determine the minimum dimension of a rational normal scroll containing the curve as a section of its ruling in terms of the minimal generators of the corresponding simultaneous annihilator. For rational curves lying as divisors on rational normal surface scrolls, we characterize their smoothness and describe the generators of their defining ideals.
item.dc:creator: Maciej Ga{\l}\k{a}zka, Jaewoo Jung, Hyunsuk Moon

item.title: Boundedness and Kawamata-Viehweg vanishing for threefolds of Fano type in large characteristics
item.description: arXiv:2611.32354v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study threefolds over algebraically closed fields of large positive characteristic. Let \((X,B)\) be a projective log canonical pair with \(X\) of Fano type, \(-(K_X+B)\) nef and coefficients of \(B\) in a fixed hyperstandard set. We obtain a monotonic complement of bounded index. For exceptional pairs the complement is Kawamata log terminal. We prove that all \(\epsilon\)-log canonical weak log Fano threefolds are arithmetically bounded above a characteristic threshold independent of \(\epsilon\). We also prove Kawamata--Viehweg vanishing for integral \(\Q\)-Cartier Weil divisors on projective threefolds of Fano type above an absolute characteristic threshold.
item.dc:creator: Xintong Jiang

item.title: An Introduction to O-minimal Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2611.32426v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: These lecture notes on o-minimal geometry comprise six chapters: 1 - O minimal Structures. 2 - Cell Decomposition. 3 - Connected Components and Dimension. 4 - Definable Triangulation. 5 - Generic Fibers for Definable Families. 6 - Smoothness.
item.dc:creator: Michel Coste

item.title: Integral Hodge/Tate conjecture of quotients via weak approximation
item.description: arXiv:2611.32494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a finite group acting on a smooth projective separably rationally connected variety over an algebraically closed field, we prove that the rational quotient map induces a surjection from the coinvariants of its second Kato homology onto the second Kato homology of any smooth projective quotient model (with coefficients invertible in the ground field). The integral Hodge and Tate conjectures for one-cycles consequently descend to such quotient models. The proof uses weak approximation over function fields to retain the image of a smooth fiber in the total space.
item.dc:creator: Yang Cao, Zhiyu Tian

item.title: Steiner porism and boundary value problems
item.description: arXiv:2611.32507v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The aim of this paper is to describe several interpretations of Steiner chains of circles in terms of certain boundary value problems and give a short review of related results. Our approach and discussion are motivated by the recent results on the geometry of Steiner porism based on an apparently novel analytic parametrization of poristic circles obtained by A.Diakvnishvili and the present author. We also mention a few feasible problems and generalizations suggested by the constructions and considerations presented in the paper. Keywords: Steiner chain of circles, Steiner porism, curvature, invariant moments of curvatures, boundary value problem, Riemann-Hilbert problem, Brylinski loop space, circle packing
item.dc:creator: Giorgi Khimshiashvili

item.title: Theta Functions and Intrinsic Mirrors of Laurent Phenomenon Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.32571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct bases of upper Laurent phenomenon algebras over a field by minimizing Newton polytopes in a single seed. For any translation-invariant total order on the exponents, each least exponent $a$ that occurs determines a smallest Newton polytope $Q_a$. Choose one element with Newton polytope $Q_a$ and least term $x^a$ for each such $a$. These elements form a basis. In every reachable seed chart, every Gauss valuation takes a nonzero basis expansion to the minimum of its values on the nonzero summands. Suppose the algebra has Laurent coefficients and smooth spectrum over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. After setting the curve parameters to one, we compute theta products on the intrinsic mirror from the exchange polynomials and give a finite presentation of the mirror algebra. A seed has a polynomial corner if each exchange polynomial can be multiplied by a unit of the coefficient ring to give a polynomial with constant term one. At such a corner, order the exponents by a weight with strictly positive, rationally independent coordinates. For every lattice exponent $a$ and integral weight $p$, the theta function indexed by $p$ has least $a$-weight $\min_{b\in Q_a}\langle b,p\rangle$ in the corresponding mirror chart. This reciprocity holds for cyclic exchanges and arbitrary pole orders. For fixed exchange supports and constant terms one, we determine when the mirror is smooth and the second mirror recovers the original algebra in the chosen torus coordinates. The coefficient tuples for which both conditions hold form a computable finite set. All their entries are positive integers.
item.dc:creator: Jiarui Fei

item.title: Uniform Algebraic Degeneracy of Entire Curves into Complex Projective Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.32597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is devoted to the algebraic degeneracy of entire curves intersecting a simple-normal-crossing divisor on smooth projective varieties over C, within the logarithmic Green-Griffiths-Lang program. For negativelytwisted global logarithmic jet differentials, we introduce an intrinsic weighted conormal filtration along each positive-dimensional closed boundary stratum, with weights prescribed by the contact orders along boundary components. Applying the maximal Harder-Narasimhan slopes of logarithmic cotangent bundles and the normal degrees of the strata, we define an integer vanishing threshold which can improve the pole bound obtained from the slope-based ceiling. Under the stable-base-locus hypothesis for the logarithmic Semple tower, we then establish an improved second main theorem whose counting coefficients depend on the boundary stratum, actual contact orders and the ratio of source weight to twisting exponent. These coefficients are independent of the powers used to realize the stable base locus. We further derive a uniform algebraicdegeneracy criterion allowing positive corrected pole coefficients, formulated via a finite system of stratumwise inequalities together with the ampleness of a residual divisor class. This yields conditional orbifold Green-Griffiths-Lang type statements. Refinements arising from conormalbundle decompositions and sharp local pole estimates at surface boundary crossings are established. Our examples exhibit strict improvement over naive slope-based bounds and illustrate that full-weight poles can persist at boundary crossings, and furnish concrete instances satisfying the stablebaselocus hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Xianjing Dong, Yanda Lv

item.title: Quasifibrations in \'etale homotopy theory
item.description: arXiv:2611.32721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study quasifibrations in \'etale homotopy theory and prove a criterion for a morphism of schemes to be a quasifibration in terms of its (higher) direct images for sheaves of sets and (possibly non-abelian) groups. This allows to generalise Friedlander's formula for the homotopy fibre of geometric fibrations to the case of an arbitrary qcqs base scheme that is not necessarily normal. Among the applications to geometric fibrations are (1) specialisation is an equivalence on the pro-$\Sigma$ completed profinite \'etale homotopy types of geometric fibres, (2) a long exact sequence of \'etale homotopy groups in characteristic 0, and (3) a partially $\Sigma$-completed exact sequence of \'etale homotopy groups in low degree terms in general.
item.dc:creator: Tim Holzschuh, Alexander Schmidt, Jakob Stix

item.title: On the generalized foliated cone theorem of rank one
item.description: arXiv:2611.32733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the cone theorem for generalized foliated quadruples of rank one in arbitrary dimension. As an application, we prove the uniqueness of MMP outputs for log canonical generalized foliated quadruples of rank one.
item.dc:creator: Mengchu Li

item.title: Line bundles on regular semisimple Hessenberg varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.32752v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a connected simply-connected simple algebraic group over $\mathbb{C}$ and $B$ be a Borel subgroup of $G$. Let $Y$ be an irreducible regular semisimple Hessenberg variety in $G/B$. In this article, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for the natural restriction map $\mathrm{res}: \mathrm{Pic}(G/B)\longrightarrow \mathrm{Pic}(Y)$ of Picard groups induced by the inclusion $Y\subseteq G/B$ to be an isomorphism.
item.dc:creator: Arkadev Ghosh, Pinakinath Saha

item.title: A Barsotti-Weil isomorphism for Taelman units
item.description: arXiv:2611.32767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The positive-characteristic analogue of motivic cohomology with coefficients in an Anderson A-motive M over a function field of transcendence degree one was introduced in an earlier work of the author. In this paper, we prove that, when M arises as the dual of the A-motive of an Anderson module E that is abelian, uniformizable, and has everywhere good reduction, the corresponding A-motivic cohomology coincides with the module of Taelman units of E, up to a twist by the module of K\"ahler differentials of A. To this end, we recast the theory of Anderson generating functions in the spirit of earlier work of Maurischat and the author on special functions.
item.dc:creator: Quentin Gazda

item.title: Semi-local Zariski-van Kampen theorems
item.description: arXiv:2611.32880v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zariski-van Kampen theorems are meant to constitute a complement to Lefschetz-Zariski theorems which, in turn, generalize the classical Lefschetz theorem on hyperplane sections to quasi-projective varieties or to the corresponding local case. Semi-local Zariski-van Kampen theorems are developed here as a tool which is useful both in the local and in the global case.
item.dc:creator: Helmut A. Hamm

item.title: Positive Geometry of Oriented Matroid Strata
item.description: arXiv:2611.32956v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the positive geometry of Grassmannians whose boundary is a union of Pl\"ucker divisors. For the full Pl\"ucker boundary the regions are closures of realization spaces of uniform oriented matroids. In rank three we show that the pair $(\mathrm{Gr}_{3,n},Z_{3,n})$ is a positive arrangement in the sense of Sturmfels and Telen for $n\le 9$ points and compute its combinatorial rank from point counts of the configuration space $\mathcal{X}_{3,n}$ over finite fields. For seven points the canonical forms of the regions span all logarithmic forms. For eight points they do not, because the M\"obius-Kantor configuration is not realizable over the reals. This determines for seven and eight points whether the integrands of Cachazo, Early and Zhang for the generalized biadjoint amplitudes of Cachazo, Early, Guevara and Mizera span the space of logarithmic forms. From ten points on, the genus is positive because a K3 surface appears in the boundary. For smaller boundaries and arbitrary rank we give a recursion that adds one point at a time and preserves the genus and the combinatorial rank. It recovers the positive Grassmannian and shows that realization spaces of stacked polytopes are regions of positive arrangements of combinatorial rank one.
item.dc:creator: Arne Kuhrs, Artyom Lisitsyn

item.title: Bloch Discriminants of Discrete Periodic Operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.33025v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Bloch variety of an operator on a periodic graph encodes the relation between its spectrum and the group action on the graph, with critical points corresponding to edges of the spectrum. We adapt methods from computational algebraic geometry to describe how the qualitative behavior of critical points of Bloch varieties depends upon parameters for three Z^2-periodic graphs. The set of parameters where the qualitative behavior changes is the Bloch discriminant. As the critical points are real-algebraic with respect to a non-standard real structure on the complex torus, this is also a first step towards developing computational tools for varieties with a non-standard real structure.
item.dc:creator: Margaret H. Regan, Frank Sottile, Simon Telen

item.title: Progress on the Stable Fields Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.31356v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that every infinite stable field of positive characteristic is separably closed. We also show that the field $\mathbb{C}(t)$ has the strict order property (hence is unstable).
item.dc:creator: G Conant, J Freitag, C Terry

item.title: Irrationality and differential equations: the work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang
item.description: arXiv:2611.31507v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Beautiful recent work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang has given new methods for proving irrationality of certain arithmetically interesting constants, notably $L(2, \chi_{-3})$, building on ideas of Siegel, Andr\'e, Bost-Charles, and others. This note is meant to explain some of this work for the 2027 JMM Current Events Bulletin, and to situate it in context of some results and conjectures in arithmetic and algebraic geometry.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Litt

item.title: Flexible algebraic curves and fake vanishing cycles
item.description: arXiv:2611.31551v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that complex curves in sufficiently ample linear systems on simply connected projective surfaces are topologically (spin) flexible: any (spin) mapping class of the underlying real surface extends to a topological mapping class of the ambient 4-manifold. As a corollary, we prove that smooth curves in the complex projective plane are topologically (spin) flexible. A consequence of topological flexibility is the existence of fake vanishing cycles, that is, simple closed curves on the underlying real surface that are not vanishing cycles, yet still bound a topologically embedded $(\pm1)$-framed disk in the surface exterior. We also give examples of pushed in Seifert surfaces in $D^4$ that are not topologically spin-flexible, but become spin-flexible after a single internal stabilization. Our methods utilize the equivariant intersection form on the surface exterior.
item.dc:creator: Joshua Lehman, Tudur Lewis

item.title: On the leading constant in Manin's conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2611.31562v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We disprove a conjecture of Batyrev and Tschinkel concerning counting rational points of bounded height. Our results strongly suggest that the transcendental Brauer group plays a role in the leading constant in problems of the same nature such as the Manin--Peyre conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Stephanie Chan, Peter Koymans, Nick Rome, Tim Santens

item.title: Tensor powers of the Steinberg character of $GL_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, zonotopal algebras, and quiver varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.31602v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we study the $m$-th tensor power ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$ of the Steinberg character of $GL_n(q)$. To do that we use the connection between tensor products of unipotent characters and the cohomology of certain quiver varieties for star-shaped quivers \cite{L2}\cite{LRV}. We prove that the cohomology ring of the quiver variety associated to ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$ is generated by its tautological classes. We use this to prove that this cohomology ring is isomorphic to a central zonotopal algebra. We then deduce a combinatorial formula for the multiplicities of unipotent characters in ${\rm St}^{\otimes m}$. This formula has been conjectured by the second author when $m=2$.
item.dc:creator: Emmanuel Letellier, Fernando Rodriguez Villegas

item.title: Linear rank-\(k\) nonincreasing and preserving maps
item.description: arXiv:2611.31807v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We characterize the linear maps between rectangular matrix spaces that carry matrices of rank at most \(k\) to matrices of rank at most \(k\). Over every field, such a map has the form \(X\mapsto MXN\) or \(X\mapsto MX\T N\), or its entire image has upper rank at most \(k\). The proof uses polynomial functions on determinantal loci and extends Loewy's infinite-field theorem to all finite fields. Over fields with more than two elements, exact preservation of rank \(k\) implies rank-\(k\) nonincrease. Over \(\F_2\), for each \(k\ge2\), we construct a rank-\(k\) preserver that sends a rank-one matrix to a matrix of rank \(k+1\). For maps whose images have upper rank \(k\), three block rank equalities characterize exact preservation. Over \(\C\), we combine the Huang--Landsberg classification with a degree obstruction on \(\mathrm{PGL}_k\) to show that every primitive core of upper rank four arising from a rank-four preserver is, up to equivalence and transposition, a projected exterior-product space on \(\C^5\). If either source dimension exceeds five, every complex rank-four preserver is standard with full-rank factors or is a compression. A \(4\times5\) example attains the bound. The degree obstruction also shows that, over any algebraically closed field, every linear map \(\M_k\to\Alt_{k+1}\) sends some invertible matrix to a matrix of rank at most \(k-2\) when \(4\mid k\).
item.dc:creator: Huajun Huang

item.title: Derivations of Low-Dimensional Filiform Lie Superalgebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.32454v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the even and odd derivations of the 91 entries in Gilg's classification list of complex filiform Lie superalgebras of superdimensions (2|2), (2|3), (2|4), (3|2), (3|3), (4|2), (5|2) and (6|2). A unified linear system yields explicit matrix parametrizations and the dimensions of both homogeneous components of the derivation superalgebra. The results are given in block-matrix form.
item.dc:creator: Muratova Kh. A., Tyan M. D

item.title: Arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas for unitary Shimura varieties with Iwahori levels
item.description: arXiv:2611.32570v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we formulate conjectural formulas for the arithmetic intersection numbers of special cycles on unitary Shimura varieties with Iwahori level structure. We first introduce a framework for formulating Kudla-Rapoport conjectures: we develop the theory of weighted representation densities and special cycles for general parahoric level structures, prove dimension-reduction formulas on both the analytic and geometric sides and duality relations for special cycles. We then formulate the Kudla-Rapoport conjecture for Iwahori level structures based on these properties. Finally, we prove the conjecture when $n=2$.
item.dc:creator: Sungyoon Cho, Qiao He, Chul-hee Lee, Zhiyu Zhang

item.title: Counting periodic points of rational self-maps of projective varieties
item.description: arXiv:2611.32875v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the number of isolated periodic points of a dominant rational self-map of a smooth projective variety. We first give an upper bound for this number in terms of the degrees of the iterates of the map, thereby extending a theorem of Dinh--Nguyen--Truong to arbitrary characteristic. Our approach is purely algebraic and bypasses the theory of densities of positive closed currents. We then establish the exact asymptotic growth of isolated periodic points of birational self-maps of surfaces over a field of characteristic 0. To do so, we extend Jonsson--Reschke's argument to any finitely generated field over $ \mathbb Q $ using Moriwaki's theory of heights.
item.dc:creator: Xiao Li

item.title: Vanishing results for the coherent cohomology of automorphic vector bundles over the Siegel variety in positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2202.06691v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove vanishing results for the coherent cohomology of the good reduction modulo $p$ of the Siegel variety with coefficients in some automorphic bundles. We show that for an automorphic bundle with highest weight $\lambda$ near the walls of the anti-dominant Weyl chamber, there is an integer $e \geq 0$ such that the cohomology is concentrated in degrees $[0, e]$. The accessible weights with our method are not necessarily regular and not necessarily $p$-small. Since our method is technical, we also provide an algorithm written in Sage that computes explicitly the vanishing results.
item.dc:creator: Thibault Alexandre

item.title: Geometric Manin's Conjecture for Fano 3-Folds
item.description: arXiv:2209.05517v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We classify families of free rational curves on all smooth Fano threefolds over the complex numbers. In particular, we prove the family of very free rational curves representing any fixed numerical curve class is either irreducible or empty. This proves Geometric Manin's Conjecture in dimension three. For general Fano threefolds of each deformation type, our results allow us to explicitly count the number of components of the moduli space of irreducible, geometrically rational curves, which may not be free, representing any numerical class.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Burke, Eric Jovinelly

item.title: Syzygies of general projections of canonical and paracanonical curves
item.description: arXiv:2407.08492v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X\subset\mathbb{P}^r$ be an integral linearly normal variety and $R=k[x_0,\cdots,x_r]$ the coordinate ring of $\mathbb{P}^r$. It is known that the syzygies of $X$ contain some geometric information. In recent years the syzygies of non-projectively normal varieties or in other words, the projection $X'$ of $X$ away from a linear subspace $W\subset\mathbb{P}^r$, were taken into considerations. Assuming that the coordinate ring of the ambient space that $X'$ lives in is $S$, there are two types of vanishing properties of the Betti diagrams of the projected varieties, the so-called $N_{d,p}^S$ and $\widetilde{N}_{d,p}$. The former one have been widely discussed for general varieties, for example by S. Kwak, Y. Choi and E. Park, while the latter one was discussed by W. Lee and E. Park for curves of very large degree. In this paper I will discuss about the $\widetilde{N}_{d,p}$ properties of the projection of a generic canonical and paracanonical curve away from a generic point and in particular whether they are cut out by quadrics. Some conjectures will be claimed based on the tests on Macaulay2.
item.dc:creator: Li Li

item.title: A smooth compactification of similarity classes of triangles
item.description: arXiv:2408.07792v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We provide a smooth algebraic compactification of the space of labeled, oriented similarity classes of triangles, as a quotient of a 3-point configuration space in the plane -- minus triple-collisions -- by the similarity group. The configuration space is naturally isomorphic to the Fulton-MacPherson space of \cite{FM94} and to the Schubert-Semple space of \cite{Semple}. The quotient is topologically a connected sum of three projective planes, and projects via blow-down to two shape spaces that have appeared in the literature: the well-known 2-sphere (\cite{Kend84}, \cite{Beh}, \cite{Montgomery}, \cite{ES15}), and the less-well-known 2-torus (\cite{BG23}). A natural action by the dihedral group $D_6$ yields a quotient stack describing absolute (unlabeled, unoriented) triangle classes.
item.dc:creator: Eric Brussel, Madeleine Goertz, Elijah Guptill, Kelly Lyle

item.title: Boundedness of complements for fibered Fano threefolds in positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2506.00553v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we prove a canonical bundle formula for Fano type fibrations and Shokurov's conjecture on boundedness of complements for Fano type threefold pairs $(X,B)$ with fibration structures in large characteristics. In particular, we prove the conjecture when $-(K_X+B)\not\equiv 0$ is nef and not big in large characteristics.
item.dc:creator: Xintong Jiang

item.title: Parke-Taylor Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2509.09323v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Parke--Taylor functions are certain rational functions on the Grassmannian of lines encoding MHV amplitudes in particle physics. For $n$ particles there are $n!$ Parke--Taylor functions, corresponding to all orderings of the particles. Linear relations between these functions have been extensively studied in the last years. We here describe all non-linear polynomial relations between these functions in a simple combinatorial way and study the variety parametrized by them, called the Parke--Taylor variety. We show that the Parke--Taylor variety is equal to the log canonical embedding of the moduli space $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{0,n}$ into $\mathbb{P}^{(n-2)!-1}$ due to Keel and Tevelev by exhibiting a concrete linear isomorphism with the realization in coordinates based on Kapranov's map. We also show that the intersection with the algebraic torus recovers the open part, $\mathcal{M}_{0,n}$. We give an explicit description of this isomorphism. Unlike the realization of the log canonical embedding by using the iterated Kapranov's map, this Parke--Taylor embedding very explicitly respects the symmetry of the $n$ marked points and is constructed in a single-step procedure, avoiding the intermediate embedding into a product of projective spaces.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Hollering, Dmitrii Pavlov

item.title: Quantum Adams operations in quasimap K-theory
item.description: arXiv:2510.09335v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We define quantum deformations of Adams operations in $K$-theory, in the framework of quasimap quantum $K$-theory. They provide $K$-theoretic analogs of the quantum Steenrod operations from equivariant symplectic Gromov--Witten theory. We verify the compatibility of these operations with the Kahler and equivariant $q$-difference module structures, provide sample computations via $\mathbb{Z}/k$-equivariant localization, and identify them with $p$-curvature operators of the Kahler $q$-difference connections as studied in Koroteev-Smirnov. We also formulate and verify a $K$-theoretic quantum Hikita conjecture at roots of unity, and propose an indirect algebro-geometric definition of quantum Steenrod operations.
item.dc:creator: Shaoyun Bai, Jae Hee Lee

item.title: A nine-line counterexample to a conjecture on the minimal degree of Jacobian relations
item.description: arXiv:2607.01985v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct two arrangements of nine lines in the complex projective plane with isomorphic intersection lattices, of weak combinatorics $(n_2,n_3,n_4)=(9,7,1)$, whose defining equations $f$ and $g$ satisfy $${\rm mdr}(f)=4,\qquad {\rm mdr}(g)=5.$$ Since $4<9/2$, this disproves a conjecture of the first author which would have implied Terao's Conjecture on the combinatorial nature of the freeness of line arrangements. Equivalently, the rank two vector bundle of logarithmic vector fields is strictly semistable for the first arrangement and stable for the second one. Hence the stability of this bundle is not determined by the intersection lattice, which gives a counterexample to a conjecture of Abe. The two arrangements also have different minimal free resolutions of their Milnor algebras. All computations are exact, and a short SINGULAR script performing them is included.
item.dc:creator: Alexandru Dimca, Piotr Pokora

item.title: Non-vanishing of the structure-sheaf cohomology of affine henselian schemes and henselian affinoids
item.description: arXiv:2609.30851v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair such that $A$ is a domain of characteristic zero and $I\ne0$. We prove that any flat affine henselian scheme of finite presentation over $(A,I)$ has nonzero first structure-sheaf cohomology whenever one of its fibers over a point in $V(I)$ has positive dimension. This in particular gives a negative answer to the question by Devadas in the mixed-characteristic case. As an application, we also prove that the first structure-sheaf cohomology does not vanish for henselian affinoids of positive dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Yoshinori Gongyo, Fumiharu Kato, Takayuki Uchiba

item.title: Transcending Algebraic Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.00335v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give an exposition of some of the ideas leading up to Jacob Tsimerman's groundbreaking work developing the theory of o-minimal definability in arithmetic and algebraic geometry.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Simpson

item.title: An explicit tame factorization of the four-variable Anick automorphism
item.description: arXiv:2610.11013v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\delta=xz-yt$. We give an explicit tame factorization of the Anick automorphism $$ f=(x+\delta t,y+\delta z,z,t) $$ of $F[x,y,z,t]$. After a linear change of coordinates, the factorization consists of sixteen elementary automorphisms, all fixing $z$. The proof uses a commutator construction with variables already present in the algebra. A complete list of the elementary factors is included in Section 5. The explicit polynomial factorization identities are defined over $Z[1/2]$; no conclusion in characteristic $2$ is asserted. We also prove that the Freudenburg--Moser-Jauslin involution $$ \tau(a,b,x,y)= \bigl(b,a,-b^3x+(1+ab+a^2b^2)y,(1-ab)x+a^3y\bigr). $$ of $F[a,b,x,y]$ is tame over every field of characteristic different from $2$ and $3$, and list an explicit factorization in Appendix.
item.dc:creator: Alexei Miasnikov, Ivan Shestakov

item.title: Free abelian group actions on projective fibered varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.25778v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $X$ be an $n$-dimensional normal projective variety of Kodaira dimension $\kappa$ and $G$ an abelian subgroup of automorphisms such that all elements of $G\backslash \{\mathrm{id}\}$ are of positive entropy. Dinh and Sibony showed that $G$ is actually free abelian of rank $\le n-\kappa-1$. In this paper, we show that after replacing $G$ by a finite-index subgroup, there exists a G-Equivariant Minimal Model Program for the pair $(X, G)$ when $\mathrm{rank}(G)=n-\kappa-1$ and $\kappa>0$, and the very general fiber of the final model is a klt Calabi-Yau surface or a $Q$-abelian variety provided that the termination of flips holds in this setting.
item.dc:creator: Sichen Li

item.title: On the Hodge conjecture for hyper-K\"ahler varieties of generalized Kummer type of dimension divisible by four
item.description: arXiv:2610.31740v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the Hodge conjecture for all hyper-K\"ahler varieties of generalized Kummer type of dimension divisible by 4 and all of their powers. To this end, we show that such hyper-K\"ahler varieties are homologically motivated by their intermediate Jacobians.
item.dc:creator: Salvatore Floccari, Lie Fu

item.title: Stable compatibility for model categories
item.description: arXiv:2611.00813v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: By introducing the notion of stable compatibility, we provide a framework in the model category theory which addresses the existence of a stable model structure on the category of modules over a monad. Exact version of such monads have been studied in the setting of triangulated categories, separately as separable monads a la Balmer in tensor triangular geometry and non-separable monads a la Dell'Ambrogio and Sanders in stable homotopy theory. By introducing stable compatibility, we explore their properties together and produce a non-separable monad in Algebraic geometry and more.
item.dc:creator: Kunal Arora, Vivek Mohan Mallick

item.title: Cycles on the universal moduli of rank 2 bundles over the hyperelliptic locus
item.description: arXiv:2611.20620v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a strong Franchetta property for the universal moduli stack of rank two vector bundles over smooth hyperelliptic curves and identify the image of the Chow ring in the cohomology of a fiber via restriction and the cycle class map as precisely the monodromy invariant cohomology classes. More precisely, for every genus $g\geq 2$, degree $d$, and hyperelliptic curve $C$ of genus $g$, we show that the restriction and the cycle class map identifies the Chow ring of the universal moduli stack with the subring of $H^* (Bun_{2,d}(C),\mathbb Q)$ generated by twisted $\kappa$-classes, which coincides with $H^{*}(Bun_{2,d}(C), \mathbb Q)^{\pi_1(\mathcal H_g,[C])}$. We use this viewpoint to give an alternative proof to a theorem of Larson in arXiv:2404.12607, and verify a conjecture of the second author in arXiv:2604.11958 in the rank $2$ case. We also give a general strategy for the higher rank cases and get some partial results in higher ranks and low genus. Finally, in Appendix A, we establish the existence of multiplicative Chow-Kunneth decompositions for the moduli space of rank 2, odd degree semi-stable bundles over low genus hyper-elliptic curves using the results developed in this paper.
item.dc:creator: Soumik Ghosh, Shubham Saha

item.title: Minimal log discrepancies are lower semicontinuous and bounded
item.description: arXiv:2611.30971v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove Ambro's conjecture stating that the minimal log discrepancies are lower semicontinuous. As a consequence, minimal log discrepancies are bounded from above by the dimension of the variety, proving a conjecture of Shokurov.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Landi

item.title: Unlikely intersections with CM abelian varieties in a family and explicit bounds for canonical heights under endomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2601.05919v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathcal{A} \rightarrow S$ be a non-isotrivial abelian scheme over a smooth irreducible curve and let $\mathcal{C} \subseteq \mathcal{A}$ be an irreducible curve, all defined over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$. In 2020, Barroero and Capuano proved that, if $\mathcal{C}$ is not contained in a proper subgroup scheme, then its intersection with the union of the flat subgroup schemes of $\mathcal{A}$ of codimension at least $2$ is finite. We complement this result by proving that, if $\mathcal{C}$ is contained neither in a fixed fiber nor in a proper flat subgroup scheme, even after a finite base change, then only finitely many points of $\mathcal{C}$ lie in a proper algebraic subgroup of a CM fiber of $\mathcal{A}$. This generalizes a previous result of Barroero for fibered powers of elliptic schemes. A key ingredient of the proof is an explicit control of canonical heights under endomorphisms: for an abelian variety $A/\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, an ample symmetric divisor $D$ and $f \in \mathrm{End}(A)$, we bound $\widehat{h}_{A,D}(f(P))$ from above and from below in terms of $\widehat{h}_{A,D}(P)$, with optimal constants given by the largest and the smallest eigenvalue of $f^{\dagger}f$, where $^{\dagger}$ is the Rosati involution associated with $D$.
item.dc:creator: Luca Ferrigno

item.title: Single-valued flat connections in several variables on arbitrary Riemann surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2602.01461v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Polylogarithms on Riemann surfaces may be constructed systematically in terms of flat connections that can enjoy various algebraic and analytic properties. In this paper, we present a single-valued and modular invariant connection ${\cal J}_\text{DHS}$ on the configuration space $\text{Cf}_n(\Sigma)$ of an arbitrary number $n$ of points on an arbitrary compact Riemann surface $\Sigma$ with or without punctures. The connection ${\cal J}_\text{DHS}$ generalizes an earlier construction for a single variable and is built out of the same integration kernels. We show that ${\cal J}_\text{DHS}$ is flat on $\text{Cf}_n(\Sigma)$. For the case without punctures, we relate it to the meromorphic multiple-valued Enriquez connection ${\cal K}_\text{E}$ in $n$ variables on the universal cover $\tilde \Sigma$ of $\Sigma$ by the composition of a gauge transformation and an automorphism of the Lie algebra in which ${\cal J}_\text{DHS}$ and ${\cal K}_\text{E}$ take values. In a companion paper, we shall establish the equivalence between the flatness of these connections and the corresponding interchange and Fay identities, for arbitrary compact Riemann surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Eric D'Hoker, Oliver Schlotterer

item.title: The coordinate ring of the universal centralizer via Demazure operators
item.description: arXiv:2604.25842v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We give a simple description of the coordinate ring of the universal centralizer associated to a simply connected semisimple group. To this end, we prove a general result on Weil restriction of affine schemes $X$ over the Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak{t}$ equipped with a compatible action of the Weyl group $W$. Specifically, we show that the coordinate ring of the scheme $\mathrm{Res}^W(X)$ of $W$-fixed points of Weil restriction of $X$ to the categorical quotient $\mathfrak{t}//W$ can be obtained from the coordinate ring of $X$ by applying Demazure operators if and only if the scheme $\mathrm{Res}^W(X)$ is integral.
item.dc:creator: Tom Gannon, Victor Ginzburg

item.title: Rigidity, flexibility, and a sign error
item.description: arXiv:2610.30976v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The documents [OAI26a, OAI26b, OAI26c] claimed to prove cases of the Hodge conjecture via homological mirror symmetry, before being withdrawn by OpenAI. We discuss the source of the error (but do not analyse the rest of the argument).
item.dc:creator: Yanki Lekili, Nick Sheridan

item.title: Uniform symmetric spectral finiteness of cones definable in o-minimal structures
item.description: arXiv:2611.13376v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Cone-constrained eigenvalues of a matrix are defined by a complementarity problem over a closed convex cone. We show that every closed convex cone that is definable in an o-minimal structure is uniformly symmetrically spectrally finite; that is, the cone spectra of symmetric matrices relative to the cone (the sets of their cone-constrained eigenvalues) have uniformly bounded cardinality. In particular, we derive explicit uniform bounds for semialgebraic cones, and the explicit uniform bound we obtain for a L\"{o}wner cone depends only on the order of the matrices in the cone. Using the uniform finiteness of cone spectra, we also show that the number of singular values relative to two closed convex cones definable in a common o-minimal structure is uniformly bounded. Finally, we provide a closed convex cone that is not definable in any o-minimal structure and for which the spectra of symmetric matrices are finite but have no uniform cardinality bound.
item.dc:creator: Mitsuhiro Nishijima

item.title: Uniquely balanced polyhedral complexes are highly connected
item.description: arXiv:2611.19866v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish higher connectivity of polyhedral complexes admitting a unique positive balanced top cycle. Our main result shows that, after quotienting by common lineality, every skeleton satisfies the corresponding higher connectivity property. The proof bounds the number of connected components surviving facet deletions by the dimension of the top-cycle space using homological and linear-algebraic arguments. As applications, we prove higher connectivity for all skeleta of arbitrary pointed polyhedral structures on tropical linear spaces of valuated matroids and Bergman fans including nonrealizable cases. These results answer questions raised by Maclagan and Yu.
item.dc:creator: Kisun Lee

item.title: Formality of finite abelian covers and Jordan blocks of the monodromy
item.description: arXiv:2611.25421v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $X$ be a connected finite-type CW-complex with a map to the circle that is surjective on fundamental groups. If $X$ is formal, the algebraic monodromy of the associated infinite cyclic cover has no Jordan block of size greater than one at the eigenvalue 1, over the rationals; formality of the $d$-fold cyclic cover rules out such blocks at the $d$-th roots of unity. We study how formality of finite abelian covers and Jordan blocks of the monodromy constrain each other. We call $X$ Alexander formal if there are no such blocks at any root of unity, rationally, nor at the eigenvalue 1 modulo any prime; this is a formality property of cochains, as DG modules over the cohomology of the circle. The complement of a central hyperplane arrangement, with its Milnor fibration, is Alexander formal exactly when the numbers of hyperplanes in its irreducible factors have no common divisor greater than 1. We also show that a CDGA graded by an abelian group, over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, is formal if and only if it is formal as a graded CDGA. Hence the strong formality of Kohno and Pajitnov implies formality of every finite abelian cover of $X$, but not conversely. Modulo $p$, eigenvalues of $p$-power order collide with 1, producing Jordan blocks that strong formality allows; the two conditions are incomparable, and all four resulting classes contain arrangement complements.
item.dc:creator: Alexander I. Suciu
